fieldInstances.reason: StratagemInfo +0x40/+0x48: the code entered to call the stratagem in, a list of 1 to 9 directions ('up', 'right', 'down', 'left'). A changed code is a Runtime-owned array; the HUD stratagem list is redrawn to match.
fieldInstances.provenance: current-build retained snapshot plus schema-labelled native ownership
fieldInstances.hudSynchronization: The HUD stratagem list draws a slot's arrows once. Whenever Runtime changes or restores the code, it redraws only that stratagem's slot with the game's own arrow data once the slot exists (once per change, never every frame). A refused redraw leaves the code applied and is retried.
fieldInstances.acknowledgementRule: A code equal to another stratagem's native code requires allow_unverified_effect: which stratagem the game calls for two equal codes is not proven.

fieldInstances.reason: The stratagem's upper-case name (loadout screen and in-mission stratagem menu). Set by naming a catalogued stratagem whose name it takes.

fieldInstances.valueSource: The name of a catalogued stratagem (listed in presentationSources.stratagems): the field takes that stratagem's own value, an existing vanilla resource the game keeps loaded. fieldInstances.hudSynchronization: The HUD stratagem list draws a slot's arrows once. fieldInstances.provenance: current-build retained snapshot plus schema-labelled native ownership
fieldInstances.hudSynchronization: The HUD stratagem list draws a slot's arrows once. Whenever Runtime changes or restores the code, it redraws only that stratagem's slot with the game's own arrow data once the slot exists (once per change, never every frame). A refused redraw leaves the code applied and is retried.
fieldInstances.acknowledgementRule: A code equal to another stratagem's native code requires allow_unverified_effect: which stratagem the game calls for two equal codes is not proven.

fieldInstances.acknowledgementReason: Wind-up (the firing charge, WeaponHeat +148/+152/+156/+160; typed FP32/FP32/FP32/UINT8): the weapon fires only once its charge reaches heat.firing_charge; holding the trigger adds heat.charge_gain_per_second per second, releasing it removes heat.charge_loss_per_second per second, and heat.reset_charge_after_shot empties it after every shot (the Quasar). The charge update and the fire gate that read these members are traced (research/windup-controls-F5FEE03DCFDB.json). Live test pending: Sickle 0 fires at once, 400 winds up about 2 s.
fieldInstances.readTimingNote: read from the type record every frame by the charge update and the fire gate: a write also changes sentries already deployed

fieldInstances.writeScope: A type-record write: this stratagem's own StratagemInfo row on this machine. Its effect reaches the Eagles (a shared cooldown and a shared rearm). The mission host applies use counts; every machine should run the same mod.
fieldInstances.semantics: "eagle_rearm" turns the stratagem's uses into charges: it holds stratagem.max_uses uses (finite), each call starts its own cooldown (stratagem.cooldown, the time between charges) on it AND on every other member of the pool (the Eagles), and calling Eagle Rearm (or its automatic call once the whole pool is empty) refills all of them at once and puts the pool on the rearm's cooldown. Charges never come back one at a time.
fieldInstances.rule: Joining needs a finite use count: an unlimited count never reaches 0 and would stop the automatic rearm of the whole pool, so it is refused (set stratagem.max_uses in the same transaction).

fieldInstances.writeScope: A type-record write: this stratagem's own StratagemInfo row on this machine. Its effect reaches the Eagles (a shared cooldown and a shared rearm). The mission host applies use counts; every machine should run the same mod.
fieldInstances.semantics: "eagle_rearm" turns the stratagem's uses into charges: it holds stratagem.max_uses uses (finite), each call starts its own cooldown (stratagem.cooldown, the time between charges) on it AND on every other member of the pool (the Eagles), and calling Eagle Rearm (or its automatic call once the whole pool is empty) refills all of them at once and puts the pool on the rearm's cooldown. Charges never come back one at a time.
fieldInstances.rule: Joining needs a finite use count: an unlimited count never reaches 0 and would stop the automatic rearm of the whole pool, so it is refused (set stratagem.max_uses in the same transaction).

fieldInstances.writeScope: A type-record write: this stratagem's own StratagemInfo row on this machine. Its effect reaches the Eagles (a shared cooldown and a shared rearm). The mission host applies use counts; every machine should run the same mod.
fieldInstances.semantics: "eagle_rearm" turns the stratagem's uses into charges: it holds stratagem.max_uses uses (finite), each call starts its own cooldown (stratagem.cooldown, the time between charges) on it AND on every other member of the pool (the Eagles), and calling Eagle Rearm (or its automatic call once the whole pool is empty) refills all of them at once and puts the pool on the rearm's cooldown. Charges never come back one at a time.
fieldInstances.rule: Joining needs a finite use count: an unlimited count never reaches 0 and would stop the automatic rearm of the whole pool, so it is refused (set stratagem.max_uses in the same transaction).
fieldInstances.acknowledgementReason: StratagemInfo +200 and its four readers are code-proven offline (research/stratagem-rearm-pool-F5FEE03DCFDB.json): a pool member's uses are refilled by Eagle Rearm and its calls share the pool's cooldown. fieldInstances.rule: Joining needs a finite use count: an unlimited count never reaches 0 and would stop the automatic rearm of the whole pool, so it is refused (set stratagem.max_uses in the same transaction).

states.resolved: The bound icon template has vector artwork; iconKey names it.
states.empty_template: An icon is bound, but its template has no vector artwork in this game build.
states.unbound: The icon library binds no icon to the native stratagem type.
states.no_native_root: No uniquely resolved native root, so no native stratagem type is known.

chain: StratagemInfo.type (member 0, ENUM_UINT32 StratagemType in the pinned type library)
StratagemType value -> native member name: game.dll enum name table, every entry length equal to the type library alias length for its value
native member name -> icon key: StratagemTypeDataTemplate DataTrigger in the icon library
icon key -> DataTemplate in the same library (vector artwork or empty)
uiIconContract.note: Tooling extracts the artwork locally from the installed game. Display names are never used to select an icon.

eagleAirstrikePatterns.rule: The value selects one of the eight native landing patterns (game.dll table: bomb count and XY offsets in metres, rotated to the attack heading around the target). Bombs per strike = the pattern's count plus a per-jet extra-bomb stat (0 by default). Only 0..7 are accepted.

presentationSources.rule: The name of a catalogued stratagem (listed in presentationSources.stratagems): the field takes that stratagem's own value, an existing vanilla resource the game keeps loaded. The field's own stratagem name is its native value; setting it back restores the original. Raw localization ids and image hashes are not accepted.

customImages.source: images/<id>.png in the mod project: a 256 x 256 non-interlaced PNG. The SDK build packs it into the mod's own archive as a complete icon family under the mod's own name; it loads with the mod at startup.
guards: every game reader of the icon member and the material and texture lookups they use are the reviewed code
the image's texture and GUI icon material are loaded, the material is exactly the icon material of its name and resolves to the texture, and no vanilla atlas sprite has its name
customImages.refusal: Otherwise the operation is refused before anything is written (ASSET_UNAVAILABLE), for example when the image is not in the mod's archive or the mod is not loaded.
